why: The question asks for three statements that store count + 1 back into count, but the answer gives none. It only makes one correct point: printing count + 1 does not change the variable. That is a single aspect with no assignment applied, so it is L1.

concepts.quote: count + 1 on its own line does not change count
concepts.why: It notes that count only changes when a value is stored back into it. It never writes count = count + 1, count += 1 or count++.
It correctly says this one call prints the value one higher than count and leaves count unchanged.

concepts.quote: shows one more, but ... does not change count
concepts.why: It correctly says output only shows a value and does not change any variable.

concepts.quote: count + 1 on its own line does not change count
concepts.why: In Java, count + 1; is not a valid expression statement, so it gives a compile error ('not a statement'). It does not run and leave count unchanged.
